en: A question tag is a short question added to a statement. Use a negative tag after a positive statement and a positive tag after a negative one. In indirect questions, use statement word order with no inversion and no do/does/did.
form: positive statement, negative tag? / negative statement, positive tag? / Could you tell me + wh-word + subject + verb
ex: You live here, don't you?
She hasn't called, has she?
Could you tell me what time it is?
cmp: Direct: Where is the bank? Indirect: Do you know where the bank is? (the verb moves after the subject).

mistakes.bad: You live here, isn't it?
mistakes.good: You live here, don't you?
mistakes.why: The tag repeats the auxiliary and matches the subject.

mistakes.bad: Could you tell me where is the bank?
mistakes.good: Could you tell me where the bank is?
mistakes.why: Indirect questions use statement word order.

mistakes.bad: Do you know what time does the train leave?
mistakes.good: Do you know what time the train leaves?
mistakes.why: Do not use does in an indirect question.

exercises.q: You live in Recife, ____?
exercises.why: Positive statement in present simple: don't you.

exercises.q: She hasn't called, ____?
exercises.why: Negative statement with has: positive tag has she.

exercises.q: I'm late, ____?
exercises.why: The tag for I am is aren't I.

exercises.q: Which indirect question is correct?
opts: Could you tell me where is the bank?
Could you tell me where the bank is?
Could you tell me where does the bank is?

exercises.q: Do you know ____ the store opens at nine?
exercises.why: Yes/no indirect questions use if or whether.

exercises.q: Let's go home, ____?
exercises.why: The tag for Let's is shall we.

exercises.q: They can swim, ____ they?
exercises.why: Positive statement, negative tag with the same modal.

exercises.q: He doesn't smoke, ____ he?
Could you tell me what time the train ____ (leave)?
exercises.why: Statement word order: the train leaves.

exercises.q: I wonder ____ she is married.
exercises.why: Use if or whether in a yes/no indirect question.

exercises.q: Você mora aqui, não é?
Você sabe onde fica o banco?
exercises.ans: Do you know where the bank is?
exercises.why: Indirect question with statement word order.

exercises.q: Você poderia me dizer que horas são?
exercises.ans: Could you tell me what time it is?
exercises.why: Indirect question: what time it is.

exercises.q: Ela não está em casa, está?
exercises.ans: She isn't at home, is she?

name: Cleft Sentences: Advanced Focus
pt: Frases clivadas colocam foco em uma parte da frase. It-cleft: 'It was the manager who approved the budget' (foco em quem) ou 'It was in Paris that I met Ana' (foco em onde). Wh-cleft: 'What I need is a long holiday'. Existem ainda 'All I want is...', 'What happened was that...' e a versão invertida 'A long holiday is what I need'. Armadilha comum: traduzir 'Foi ele que...' com 'was him that' ou esquecer o that/who, e usar 'All what I want'. Depois de what-cleft com verbo de ação, o verbo seguinte fica no infinitivo: 'What she did was resign'.
en: Cleft sentences split one idea into two clauses to put focus on one part. Use it + be + focus + that/who, or a wh-clause + be + focus. Use 'All (that) I...' for 'only'.
form: It + be + focus + that/who... / What + subject + verb + be + focus
ex: It was in Paris that I met Ana.
What I need is a good rest.
What happened was that the power went out.
cmp: It-clefts focus on who, where or when. Wh-clefts focus on the thing, the action or the result.

mistakes.bad: All what I want is peace.
mistakes.good: All I want is peace.
mistakes.why: Do not add what after all.

mistakes.bad: What she did was resigned without notice.
mistakes.good: What she did was resign without notice.
mistakes.why: After 'What ... did was', use the base form or to-infinitive.

mistakes.bad: What I need are a long holiday.
mistakes.good: What I need is a long holiday.
mistakes.why: A what-clause takes a singular verb with a singular focus.

exercises.q: It was the manager ____ approved the budget.
exercises.why: A person as subject in an it-cleft: who.

exercises.q: What I need ____ a long holiday.
exercises.why: What-cleft with a singular focus: is.

exercises.q: What she did ____ to resign without notice.
Which sentence emphasises WHERE they met?
opts: It was Ana that I met in Paris.
It was in Paris that I met Ana.
What I met was Ana in Paris.
exercises.why: The focus phrase comes right after It was.

exercises.q: Which sentence is correct?
opts: All I want is a quiet evening.
All what I want is a quiet evening.
All I want are a quiet evening.
exercises.why: All + clause + is, with no what.

exercises.q: What happened ____ that the power went out.
It was my sister ____ told me the news.
exercises.why: A person as subject: who or that.

exercises.q: ____ I really enjoyed was the soundtrack.
What we should do ____ talk to the client directly.
It was not until midnight ____ the guests left.
exercises.why: It was not until + time + that.

exercises.q: Foi o gerente quem aprovou o orçamento.
exercises.ans: It was the manager who approved the budget.

exercises.q: O que eu preciso é de um bom descanso.
exercises.ans: What I need is a good rest.

exercises.q: Foi em 2019 que nos conhecemos.
exercises.ans: It was in 2019 that we met.

exercises.q: Tudo o que eu quero é paz e sossego.
exercises.ans: All I want is peace and quiet.

name: Subjunctive and Formal Structures
pt: Em inglês formal, depois de verbos como suggest, recommend, insist, demand, propose e de adjetivos como essential, vital, important, usamos that + sujeito + verbo na forma base, sem -s e sem to: 'I suggest that he go', 'It is vital that she be here'. A negação é 'not + verbo base'. Armadilha comum: usar infinitivo como no português ('Ele sugeriu mim to go'; 'exigiu ele to pay') ou conjugar o verbo ('that he pays'). Também: 'as if he were' (were para todas as pessoas) e 'Be that as it may' (seja como for).
en: After verbs of suggestion, demand or recommendation, and after adjectives like essential or vital, formal English uses that + subject + base verb. The verb does not change for person or tense.
form: suggest/insist/demand/recommend + that + subject + base verb; It is vital that + subject + base verb
ex: The doctor recommended that he get more rest.
It is essential that every employee submit the form.
She talks as if she were the boss.
cmp: Normal: He suggests that Tom goes. Formal subjunctive: He suggests that Tom go. Both are used, but the second is formal.

mistakes.bad: She suggested me to take a taxi.
mistakes.good: She suggested that I take a taxi.
mistakes.why: Suggest is not followed by object + to-infinitive.

mistakes.bad: I demand that he is here at once.
mistakes.good: I demand that he be here at once.
mistakes.why: The subjunctive uses the base form be.

mistakes.bad: It is vital that nobody doesn't be late.
mistakes.good: It is vital that nobody be late.
mistakes.why: No do-support in the subjunctive, and no double negative.

exercises.q: The doctor recommended that he ____ more rest.
It is essential that every employee ____ the form by Friday.
In formal English: It is vital that nobody ____ late.
exercises.why: Subjunctive uses the base form be.

exercises.q: Which sentence is correct?
opts: She suggested that I take a taxi.
She suggested me to take a taxi.
She suggested me taking a taxi.

exercises.q: He talks as if he ____ the boss.
'Be that as it may' means:
exercises.why: It accepts a point but moves on to another.

exercises.q: The judge ordered that the defendant ____ (pay) a fine.
I demand that he ____ (be) here at once.
It is important that she ____ (not/forget) her passport.
The committee proposed that the meeting ____ (postpone) until May.
Ele insistiu que ela pagasse a conta.
exercises.ans: He insisted that she pay the bill.

exercises.q: É essencial que todos cheguem a tempo.
exercises.ans: It is essential that everyone arrive on time.

exercises.q: Ela sugeriu que eu tomasse um táxi.
exercises.ans: She suggested that I take a taxi.

exercises.q: Ele fala como se fosse o dono.
exercises.ans: He talks as if he were the owner.

name: Advanced Articles and Determiners
pt: Sem artigo: generalizações com substantivos incontáveis ou plurais ('Life is difficult', 'Dogs are loyal'). Com 'the': coisas únicas, superlativos, ordinais, 'the + adjetivo' para grupos (the rich, the poor), países no plural ou com Republic/Kingdom (the Netherlands, the United States), instrumentos musicais (play the piano). Instituições usadas pela função não levam artigo (in hospital, at school – inglês britânico). Armadilha comum: dizer 'The life is difficult' ou 'I love the music', copiando 'A vida é difícil'. Determinantes: each/every/both/either/neither, 'the whole day' (não 'whole the day'), 'What a beautiful view!'.
en: Use no article for general ideas with plural or uncountable nouns. Use the for unique things, superlatives, groups like the rich, and some place names. Choose the right determiner: each, every, both, either, neither, the whole.
form: the + superlative / the + adjective / the whole + singular noun / What a(n) + adjective + noun
ex: Life is difficult sometimes.
She spent the whole day studying.
What a beautiful view!
cmp: 'I love music' is music in general. 'I love the music in this film' is a specific one.

mistakes.bad: The life is full of surprises.
mistakes.good: Life is full of surprises.
mistakes.why: No article for a general abstract noun.

mistakes.bad: She spent whole the day reading.
mistakes.good: She spent the whole day reading.
mistakes.why: The whole: the comes first.

mistakes.bad: What beautiful view!
mistakes.good: What a beautiful view!
mistakes.why: What + a + adjective + singular countable noun.

exercises.q: ____ life is full of surprises.
exercises.why: No article for a general abstract noun.

exercises.q: Of all the cities I visited, Lisbon was ____ best.
In British English, 'My brother is in hospital' means:
opts: He works there as a doctor.
exercises.why: No article: the institution is used for its purpose.

exercises.q: What ____ beautiful view!
____ of my two brothers lives in Canada.
exercises.why: Each of + plural noun takes a singular verb.

exercises.q: She spent ____ day reading.
I'd like ____ umbrella, please.
We visited ____ Netherlands last summer.
exercises.why: The Netherlands is a plural name.

exercises.q: She plays ____ piano very well.
The rich ____ not always happy.
A vida é difícil às vezes.
exercises.why: No article for a general abstract noun.

exercises.q: Que vista linda!
Ela passou o dia inteiro estudando.
exercises.ans: She spent the whole day studying.

exercises.q: Eles moram nos Estados Unidos.
exercises.ans: They live in the United States.

name: Emphasis and Contrast Structures
pt: Para dar ênfase, use do/does/did antes do verbo base em frases afirmativas: 'I do like your plan' (eu realmente gosto). Para contraste: although/even though + oração ('Although he was tired, he kept working'); despite/in spite of + substantivo ou -ing ('Despite the rain...'); whereas/while para comparar dois fatos; however em outra frase, entre vírgulas ou depois de ponto e vírgula. Armadilhas comuns: 'Although..., but...' (em inglês, só um conectivo), 'despite of' (o certo é despite ou in spite of) e 'Despite he was tired'.
en: Use do/does/did + base verb to emphasise a positive statement. Contrast with although + clause, despite + noun/-ing, whereas for two opposite facts, and however to start a new idea.
form: do/does/did + base verb / although + clause / despite + noun or -ing / ..., whereas ... / ; however,
ex: I do like your plan, but it is too expensive.
Although he was tired, he kept working.
Despite the rain, we went out.
cmp: Although is followed by a clause. Despite is followed by a noun or -ing. However is a linking adverb, not a conjunction.

mistakes.bad: Although he was tired, but he kept working.
mistakes.good: Although he was tired, he kept working.
mistakes.why: Do not use although and but together.

mistakes.bad: Despite of the rain, we went out.
mistakes.good: Despite the rain, we went out.
mistakes.why: Despite is never followed by of; in spite of is the longer form.

mistakes.bad: Despite it was raining, we went out.
mistakes.good: Although it was raining, we went out.
mistakes.why: Despite cannot be followed by a full clause.

exercises.q: I ____ like your plan, but it is too expensive.
She ____ call you yesterday; maybe she used the wrong number.
____ it was raining, we went for a walk.
____ the rain, we went out.
exercises.why: Despite is followed by a noun.

exercises.q: Which sentence is correct?
opts: Although he was tired, he kept working.
Although he was tired, but he kept working.
Despite of being tired, he kept working.
exercises.why: Use only one contrast connector and no 'of' after despite.

exercises.q: My sister loves coffee, ____ I prefer tea.
He ____ say sorry, but nobody believed him.
____ the traffic, we arrived on time.
exercises.why: Despite or in spite of before a noun.

exercises.q: I like cats; ____, my brother prefers dogs.
exercises.why: However links two sentences, after a semicolon.

exercises.q: ____ she studied hard, she failed the exam.
exercises.why: Although introduces a clause of contrast.

exercises.q: Embora estivesse cansado, ele continuou trabalhando.
exercises.ans: Although he was tired, he kept working.

exercises.q: Apesar da chuva, nós saímos.
exercises.ans: Despite the rain, we went out.

exercises.q: Eu realmente gosto do seu plano.
Ela é rica; no entanto, não é feliz.
exercises.ans: She is rich; however, she is not happy.
exercises.why: however after a semicolon, followed by a comma.

name: Hedging & Diplomatic Language
pt: Em reuniões e e-mails corporativos, ser direto demais soa ríspido. Use hedging (suavização) para discordar ou pedir mudanças com elegância: "tend to", "seem to", "it appears that", "I was wondering if", "would you mind", "could we possibly", "a bit / slightly". Em vez de "You are wrong", diga "I see your point, though I'm not sure that works here".
en: Soften claims, requests, and disagreements in professional settings using hedging verbs (seem, tend, appear), modal past forms (could, might, would), and softeners (slightly, a bit, I was wondering if).
form: I was wondering if + could; It seems/tends to + verb; Would you mind + -ing; Not quite / slightly
ex: I was wondering if we could push the deadline back by two days.
The new rollout tends to slow down older devices slightly.
With all due respect, I am not sure that timeline is realistic.
cmp: Direct: "Change this slide." Diplomatic: "Would you mind adjusting this slide slightly before the client call?"

mistakes.bad: I was wondering if you can send the file.
mistakes.good: I was wondering if you could send the file.
mistakes.why: Pair "I was wondering if" with past-tense modals (could/would) for polite distance.

mistakes.bad: Would you mind to open the window?
mistakes.good: Would you mind opening the window?
mistakes.why: "Would you mind" is followed by -ing, never "to + verb".

exercises.q: I was wondering if we ____ reschedule the review for Thursday.
exercises.why: Use "could" after "I was wondering if" for polite requests.

exercises.q: Would you mind ____ the client summary before noon?
exercises.why: "Would you mind" always takes the -ing form.

exercises.q: Which sentence sounds most diplomatic in a meeting?
opts: I see what you mean, though that estimate seems slightly optimistic.
You do not know the numbers.
exercises.why: Acknowledging the other view and using "seems slightly" softens disagreement.

exercises.q: Large attachments ____ slow down our email server during peak hours.
exercises.why: "Tend to" hedges a general claim without sounding absolute.

exercises.q: ____ be possible to review the contract one more time?
exercises.why: "Would it be possible to..." is a standard polite opener.

exercises.q: I was ____ (wonder) if you could share the latest budget.
exercises.why: "I was wondering if..." is the fixed polite request frame.

exercises.q: Would you mind ____ (send) me the slides after the call?
Users ____ (tend) to abandon forms that ask for too many fields.
The timeline looks ____ (slight) tight for a full security audit.
exercises.why: Use the adverb "slightly" before an adjective ("slightly tight").

exercises.q: It ____ (appear) that two teams worked on the same ticket.
exercises.why: "It appears/seems that..." reports a finding cautiously.

exercises.q: Eu gostaria de saber se poderíamos adiar a reunião.
exercises.ans: I was wondering if we could postpone the meeting.
exercises.why: I was wondering if + subject + could + base verb.

exercises.q: Você se importaria de revisar este parágrafo?
exercises.ans: Would you mind reviewing this paragraph?

exercises.q: Essa abordagem parece um pouco arriscada.
exercises.ans: That approach seems a bit risky.

exercises.q: Com todo o respeito, não tenho certeza se isso funciona.
exercises.ans: With all due respect, I am not sure that works.
exercises.why: Fixed diplomatic opener before a polite disagreement.

name: Discourse Markers & Stance
pt: Em nível C1, marcadores de discurso mostram sua postura e estruturam argumentos complexos: "admittedly" (reconheço que), "needless to say" (nem precisa dizer), "broadly speaking" (em linhas gerais), "that said" (dito isso), "on the contrary" (pelo contrário), "by and large" (no geral). Armadilha: não confunda "on the other hand" (outro lado da moeda) com "on the contrary" (negação direta).
en: Use C1 stance and discourse markers to frame arguments, concede points, and pivot cleanly: admittedly, that said, broadly speaking, by and large, on the contrary, nonetheless.
form: Admittedly, ...; Broadly speaking, ...; That said, ...; On the contrary, ...
ex: Admittedly, the migration took longer than we had planned.
Broadly speaking, small models perform well on classification tasks.
The budget is tight; that said, we can still ship the core features.
cmp: "On the other hand" balances two sides; "On the contrary" rejects the previous claim as false.

mistakes.bad: The app is slow. On the contrary, it is cheap.
mistakes.good: The app is slow. On the other hand, it is cheap.
mistakes.why: "On the contrary" contradicts the previous claim; "on the other hand" introduces a contrasting advantage.

mistakes.bad: By and large, I totally disagree with every single word.
mistakes.good: By and large, the new process works well.
mistakes.why: "By and large" means "generally / on the whole", not "strongly".

exercises.q: ____, the initial setup is complex, yet the daily workflow is effortless.
exercises.why: "Admittedly" concedes a drawback before presenting the positive side.

exercises.q: "Did the outage hurt sales?" — "____, conversions actually rose this week."
exercises.why: "On the contrary" directly contradicts a negative assumption.

exercises.q: The tool is not cheap. ____, it saves the team ten hours every week.
exercises.why: "That said" pivots to a balancing point after acknowledging a limitation.

exercises.q: ____, European clients expect stricter data guarantees than US startups.
____, the merger went smoothly despite a few tense weeks in HR.
exercises.why: "By and large" means "overall / on the whole".

exercises.q: ____ (admit), we underestimated how much testing the API needed.
exercises.why: Use the sentence adverb "Admittedly" to concede a point.

exercises.q: ____ (need) to say, unencrypted backups are unacceptable.
exercises.why: "Needless to say" means something is obvious.

exercises.q: The timeline is ambitious; ____ (nonetheless / however) we met every milestone.
exercises.why: Both "nonetheless" and "however" work after a semicolon.

exercises.q: ____ (broad) speaking, automation reduces human error.
Two teams led the project, ____ (name) Platform and Security.
exercises.why: "Namely" specifies the exact items just mentioned.

exercises.q: Reconhecidamente, o prazo foi curto demais.
exercises.ans: Admittedly, the deadline was too tight.

exercises.q: Dito isso, ainda podemos entregar na sexta.
exercises.ans: That said, we can still deliver on Friday.

exercises.q: No geral, os usuários aprovaram a mudança.
exercises.ans: By and large, users approved the change.
exercises.why: By and large + comma + main clause.

exercises.q: Nem precisa dizer que a segurança vem primeiro.
exercises.ans: Needless to say, security comes first.
exercises.why: Needless to say + comma + main clause.

name: Nominalization in Formal Writing
pt: Nominalização é transformar verbos e adjetivos em substantivos para deixar relatórios, e-mails executivos e textos acadêmicos mais concisos e objetivos: "We decided to expand" → "The decision to expand"; "Because the server failed" → "Following the server failure"; "How fast they responded" → "The speed of their response".
en: Turn verbs and adjectives into noun phrases to write concise, formal executive summaries and reports: "the implementation of", "a sharp rise in", "following the failure of".
form: Verb/Adj → Noun phrase + of/in (e.g. "implementing X" → "the implementation of X")
ex: The implementation of two-factor login reduced account takeovers by 80%.
Following the delay in shipping, customer complaints rose sharply.
Their reluctance to share logs slowed down the audit.
cmp: Conversational: "Because they failed to test it, the site crashed." Formal: "The failure to test it resulted in a site crash."

mistakes.bad: The implement of the policy took weeks.
mistakes.good: The implementation of the policy took weeks.
mistakes.why: Use the noun "implementation", not the verb "implement".

mistakes.bad: There was a sharp grow in traffic.
mistakes.good: There was a sharp growth in traffic.
mistakes.why: Use the noun "growth" after "a sharp".

exercises.q: The ____ of strict access controls prevented further leaks.
Which sentence uses nominalization naturally for an executive report?
opts: We complained because the delivery was late.
The delay in delivery led to several customer complaints.
exercises.why: "The delay in delivery" and "customer complaints" pack actions into clear noun phrases.

exercises.q: His ____ to compromise stalled the negotiations for weeks.
There has been a steady ____ in remote engineering roles.
exercises.why: "A steady growth in..." is the natural nominalized pattern.

exercises.q: The ____ of the new pricing model sparked lively debate.
exercises.why: "The introduction of..." uses the noun form.

exercises.q: The ____ (fail) to back up the database proved costly.
We noticed a significant ____ (improve) in response times.
Their ____ (decide) to postpone the launch was wise.
The ____ (analyze) of recent logs revealed a memory leak.
Lack of ____ (clear) in the brief caused rework.
A implementação da nova regra levou duas semanas.
exercises.ans: The implementation of the new rule took two weeks.
exercises.why: The + noun + of + noun phrase + verb.

exercises.q: O atraso na entrega gerou reclamações.
exercises.ans: The delay in delivery caused complaints.

exercises.q: A recusa deles em assinar surpreendeu a diretoria.
exercises.ans: Their refusal to sign surprised the board.

exercises.q: Houve uma queda acentuada nos custos.
exercises.ans: There was a sharp drop in costs.
exercises.why: There was + a + adj + noun + in + noun.

name: Advanced Conditionals & Alternatives to If
pt: No C1, você varia além do "if": "provided (that) / as long as" (desde que), "unless" (a menos que), "in case" (caso/por precaução), "otherwise" (senão), e inversão sem "if" ("Should you need...", "Were we to launch...", "Had they tested..."). Armadilha: "in case" significa prevenção (não é sinônimo de "if"), e "unless" nunca leva verbo negativo depois.
en: Replace basic "if" with provided that, as long as, unless, in case, otherwise, and inverted conditionals (Should you..., Were it not for..., Had we...).
form: Provided (that) / As long as + clause; Were it not for + noun; Had + S + V3
ex: We can ship on Friday, provided that all integration tests pass.
Were it not for the automated backup, we would have lost everything.
Should you notice any suspicious logins, revoke the session immediately.
cmp: "Take a charger in case the battery dies" (precaution). "Charge it if the battery is low" (condition).

mistakes.bad: Unless you don't hurry, we will miss the train.
mistakes.good: Unless you hurry, we will miss the train.
mistakes.why: "Unless" already means "if not"; never use another negative.

mistakes.bad: If I would have known, I had called you.
mistakes.good: Had I known, I would have called you.
mistakes.why: Formal 3rd conditional inversion: Had + subject + V3, ... would have + V3.

exercises.q: We will renew the contract, ____ they match our security requirements.
exercises.why: "Provided that" means "only if / on condition that".

exercises.q: ____ you need any help during onboarding, feel free to message me.
exercises.why: "Should you need..." is a polite C1 equivalent of "If you happen to need...".

exercises.q: ____ it not for her quick reaction, the outage would have lasted hours.
exercises.why: "Were it not for..." means "If it weren't for...".

exercises.q: Keep a copy of the passport on your phone ____ you lose the physical one.
exercises.why: "In case" expresses precaution for a possible future event.

exercises.q: Rotate the keys today; ____, the build pipeline will expire tomorrow.
exercises.why: "Otherwise" introduces the consequence of not doing the first action.

exercises.q: ____ (should) the server fail again, switch traffic to the secondary node.
exercises.why: 1st-conditional inversion starts with "Should + subject + base verb".

exercises.q: ____ (have) we checked the logs earlier, we would have spotted the bug.
You can work remotely ____ (long) as you join the morning stand-up.
____ (were) we to cut the price by half, margins would collapse.
Do not merge the branch ____ (unless / if) two reviewers approve it.
Caso precise de ajuda, me avise.
exercises.ans: Should you need help, let me know.

exercises.q: Se não fosse pelo backup, teríamos perdido tudo.
exercises.ans: Were it not for the backup, we would have lost everything.
exercises.why: Were it not for + noun phrase, would have + V3.

exercises.q: Aprovamos o plano, desde que o custo caia.
exercises.ans: We approve the plan, provided that the cost drops.

exercises.q: Tivéssemos testado antes, o erro não teria acontecido.
exercises.ans: Had we tested earlier, the error would not have happened.
exercises.why: Had + subject + V3, would not have + V3.

name: Fronting & Rhetorical Emphasis
pt: Para dar destaque em apresentações, discursos ou textos C1, movemos o elemento principal para o início da frase (fronting) ou usamos estruturas enfáticas: "What strikes me is...", "Much as I admire...", "Strange as it may seem...", "The last thing we need is...".
en: Bring key ideas to the front of the sentence for rhetorical impact: "Much as I respect...", "Strange though it may sound...", "The last thing we need is...", "What really matters is...".
form: Adj + as/though + S + may seem; Much as + S + V; The last thing + S + V + is
ex: Much as I respect his experience, I disagree with this timeline.
Strange though it may sound, slowing down actually helped us ship faster.
The last thing we need right now is an unannounced pricing change.
cmp: Neutral: "Although it seems strange, it worked." Emphatic: "Strange as it may seem, it worked."

mistakes.bad: As strange it may seem, the bug vanished.
mistakes.good: Strange as it may seem, the bug vanished.
mistakes.why: Put the adjective BEFORE "as/though": "Strange as it may seem".

mistakes.bad: Much as I like coffee, but I stopped.
mistakes.good: Much as I like coffee, I stopped.
mistakes.why: Never use "but" after a "Much as..." concessive clause.

exercises.q: ____ as it may seem, deleting half the features doubled user retention.
exercises.why: Use Adjective + as + subject + may seem.

exercises.q: ____ as I appreciate your offer, I have decided to stay in my current role.
exercises.why: "Much as I appreciate..." is a fixed C1 concessive opener.

exercises.q: The ____ thing we want is another outage during Black Friday.
exercises.why: "The last thing we want/need is..." emphasizes what we strongly want to avoid.

exercises.q: ____ really matters in negotiations is listening before making an offer.
exercises.why: Use "What" to front the main point.

exercises.q: Hard ____ he tried, he could not reproduce the bug locally.
exercises.why: Use "Adverb/Adj + though/as + subject + verb", never "although" in this position.

exercises.q: ____ (much) as I admire her work, the proposal needs revisions.
Difficult ____ (as / although) it was, the team delivered on schedule.
exercises.why: Use "as" or "though" after a fronted adjective.

exercises.q: The ____ (last) thing we need is a rushed security patch.
exercises.why: "The last thing we need is..." expresses strong avoidance.

exercises.q: ____ (surprise) as it may sound, the simplest fix won.
exercises.why: Adjective "Surprising" goes before "as it may sound".

exercises.q: What ____ (strike) me most was how calm she stayed.
exercises.why: "What struck me most was..." (past tense matches "was").

exercises.q: Por mais estranho que pareça, o teste passou.
exercises.ans: Strange as it may seem, the test passed.
exercises.why: Adjective + as + it may seem, main clause.

exercises.q: Por mais que eu goste da ideia, custa caro demais.
exercises.ans: Much as I like the idea, it costs too much.
exercises.why: Much as + subject + verb, main clause.

exercises.q: A última coisa de que precisamos é outro atraso.
exercises.ans: The last thing we need is another delay.
exercises.why: The last thing + subject + need + is + noun.

exercises.q: Por mais difícil que fosse, eles não desistiram.
exercises.ans: Hard though it was, they did not give up.
exercises.why: Hard + though + it was, main clause.
